title: Example Demo: The Blueprint
subtitle: A placeholder demo that shows and explains how an interactive demo is structured
description: Placeholder demo with no subject content: it shows the blueprint of a good interactive demo — controls, visualization, observing, understanding.

intro.title: This is a placeholder demo
intro.text: This page teaches no subject matter — it shows you the blueprint. Every section is one building block of a good interactive demo and explains itself. Use this page as the template to copy for your own demos.

demo.title: Interactive Core
demo.lead: The interactive core is the heart of every demo: a visualization that reacts to your input immediately. Here it is deliberately content-free — colored dots reacting to a slider, a select, and buttons.
demo.canvasAria: Visualization area: colored dots reacting to the controls

controls.reducedMotion: Your system prefers reduced motion, so the animation is off. All controls keep working.

status.reset: Demo reset to its initial state.

tooltip.points: How many dots are drawn. A slider suits continuous quantities with a clear minimum and maximum.
tooltip.pattern: How the dots are arranged. A select suits a few clearly named variants.

structure.title: How a Demo Is Built
structure.intro: Almost every good interactive demo consists of the same four building blocks — and the learner experiences them in this order.

controls.title: Controls
controls.text: Few, clearly labeled controls: a slider for quantities, a select for variants, start/pause, and a reset. Every element carries a label, an aria-label, and an info tooltip where needed.

viz.title: Visualization
viz.text: An area that reacts to every input immediately. Essentials: a text fallback for high-contrast mode, a live region for screen readers, and respect for reduced motion.

observe.title: Observe
observe.text: The learner plays with the controls and sees the effect immediately. Short prompts guide attention: what happens when you switch the pattern? What does the slider change?

understand.title: Understand
understand.text: Finally, the observations get framed: explanatory text, a checkpoint for self-testing, and key takeaways. Only this step turns playing into learning.

checkpoint.title: Check: Got the Blueprint?
checkpoint.item1: I can name the four building blocks of a demo: controls, visualization, observing, understanding.

takeaways.title: Key Takeaways
takeaways.text:
1. **Four building blocks**: controls, visualization, observing, understanding — every demo on this page follows this order.

2. **Immediate feedback**: every input has an immediately visible effect — that is the difference between a demo and a diagram.

3. **Accessibility built in**: aria-labels, a live region, a high-contrast text fallback, and reduced motion belong in from the start, not as an afterthought.

This placeholder demo is deliberately content-free — replace the dot canvas with your own subject and keep the structure.

build.title: Build Your Own Demo
build.text: This page is the template: replace the interactive core with your subject matter and keep the structure. In development mode, two tools help you:
build.designWorkshop: the design workshop with every kit component to try out
build.newComponent: the guided way to add a new reusable component properly
